result.summary: Review of durable events/SSE replay/cursors at target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895. Verdict FINDINGS. HIGH src/http.ts:45 (root cause src/security.ts:43-50,:7): GET /events redacts each event via a lazy secrets thunk, so every string field re-runs store.all() (SELECT body + JSON.parse of every worker, each embedding a prompt up to 32KB). A 100-event page = 300 table scans: 529ms blocked event loop at the default 50 workers, 4.2s at 200; reconnect-polling burned 951% of one core, stalling MCP, the tick and /health. MEDIUM src/coordinator.ts:119 (deadline checked only at :141/:160): wait_for_state_change drains the unindexed, never-pruned events table before honouring its timeout, so timeout_ms=0 does a full scan (74ms/100k, 1200ms/1.6M). Replay verified exact: 301 events via Last-Event-ID gave 301/301, 0 dupes, 0 missing, monotonic. Tests: 22 pass/0 fail on wait/http/api/restart, Bun 1.4.2. Artifacts: .swarmforge/artifacts/review.md, findings.json.
result.details:
Target verified in a disposable detached clone at /tmp/rv13/sw (git rev-parse HEAD = d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895); /workspace/repo left at assigned baseline 5672ead, clean. Scope: src/store.ts, src/http.ts, Coordinator.waitForStateChange, GET /events, get_worker_logs pagination, redactor on the event path, runtime event log flush.

FINDING 1 HIGH src/http.ts:45, root cause src/security.ts:43-50 and :7. redactorFor returns a Redactor whose secrets is a thunk; text() calls this.secrets() on every invocation and value() recurses into every string field. Each evaluation runs c.store.all() = SELECT body FROM workers + JSON.parse of every row, and every worker body embeds a prompt of up to 32000 chars (src/domain.ts:33). http.ts:45 redacts up to 100 events x 3 string fields = 300 table scans and 300 full JSON parses. Trigger: any authenticated GET /events with a non-empty first page; the documented retry:2000 makes a browser EventSource poll forever. Reproduced with Bun 1.4.2 and local fakes: default 50 workers, 32KB prompts = 1634620 body bytes, GET /events x3 = 1588ms (529ms/request) vs 0ms for the same query without the redactor, and exactly 300 store.all() calls per 100-event page. Scaling 133/786/2001/4225ms at 25/50/100/200 workers. 6s of reconnect-polling burned 5704ms of event loop (951% of one core). Bun is single-threaded, so this stalls MCP, the 2000ms coordinator tick and /health; SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN is optional (src/config.ts:81). Existing guards bound only the query (after check :35-41, LIMIT 100 at :43), not the redaction; the per-request redactorFor at :42 snapshots nothing. No test covers /events under volume (grep /events tests/ is empty). Fix: resolve the secret array once per request and close over it, or memoize the thunk per request.

FINDING 2 MEDIUM src/coordinator.ts:119, deadline checked only at :141 and :160. next() loops lifecycleEvents(cursor, filter, 200) until match or exhaustion, so a non-matching states filter or stale cursor forces a full-table scan regardless of timeout_ms; timeout_ms=0 is documented as checks once. Reproduced: 100k events 74ms, 400k 289ms, 1.6M 1200ms at timeoutMs 0. events has no retention (OBSERVABILITY.md:30 assigns pruning to the operator) and no index (PRAGMA index_list(events) empty), so the drain grows unbounded. tests/wait.test.ts:135-160 uses only small backlogs. Fix: thread the deadline into next() and break the batch loop on expiry returning the consumed cursor; add CREATE INDEX events_worker_id ON events(worker_id, id), which also fixes metrics.ts:102/113/125.

VERIFIED CORRECT, not defects: SSE replay exact under truncation (301 events via Last-Event-ID: 100/100/100/1 then empty, 301/301 delivered, 0 dupes, 0 missing, monotonic, cursors interchangeable with wait_for_state_change both ways); cursor validation rejects abc/-1/1.5/>2^53 with 400; next_cursor on timeout is fully consumed so filtered waits cannot skip other filters events; transition() is idempotent per state so duplicate completion cannot duplicate events or tokens; listener lifecycle returns listenerCount to 0 on every exit path; /events is a finite 200 consistent with the documented bounded-replay model; event payloads carry no prompt.

LIMITATIONS: single shared-CPU container, so absolute ms differ though scaling and the 300-call count are deterministic; finding 1 worst case assumes max prompts (200B prompts at 50 workers = 57ms/request, still linear); finding 2 1.6M is a synthetic bound; the metrics index claim rests on EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN plus a 200k-event render (15ms); no concurrency test of the waiter against a busy coordinator tick. 24 probes disclosed under /tmp/rv13/probe; logs in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rv13-targeted.log and rv13-probes.log. No credentials in any output.

warnings: Finding 1 performance numbers are from one shared-CPU container; absolute milliseconds vary, but the linear scaling and the exact 300 store.all() calls per 100-event page are deterministic.
Finding 1 worst case assumes maximum-size prompts (32KB); with 200-byte prompts at the default 50 workers the cost is 57ms/request and remains linear in retained workers.
Finding 2's 1.6M-event figure is a synthetic upper bound, not a measured production backlog; real severity depends on how large the operator's events table becomes.
The events table has no index at all (PRAGMA index_list(events) empty), which also affects the per-worker scans in metrics.ts; that claim rests on EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN plus a 200k-event render (15ms).
Snapshot Bun is 1.3.14 and cannot read lockfileVersion 2; official Bun 1.4.2 was used from /tmp and the lockfile was never rewritten.
result.followup_reason: Two actionable defects in the reviewed scope need an implementation pass. HIGH (src/http.ts:45, root cause src/security.ts:43-50 and :7): the Redactor secrets thunk re-runs store.all() (full workers table SELECT + JSON.parse, each row embedding a prompt of up to 32KB) once per string field per event, so one 100-event /events page costs 300 table scans and blocks the single-threaded event loop for 529ms at the default 50 workers and 4.2s at 200; a continuously reconnecting SSE consumer pins the whole control plane (951% of one core measured). Snapshot the secret list once per request. MEDIUM (src/coordinator.ts:119, deadline checked only at :141 and :160): wait_for_state_change drains the entire unindexed, never-pruned events table before honouring its own timeout, so the documented 'timeout_ms=0 checks once' performs a full scan (1200ms at 1.6M events); thread the deadline into next() and add CREATE INDEX events_worker_id ON events(worker_id, id). Both reproduced locally with fakes only; no credentials involved.
